definition: a departure from what is normal or expected
example: The single typo was an aberration in an otherwise flawless essay.

definition: to leave hurriedly and secretly to escape custody
example: The cashier absconded with the daily receipts.

definition: the ability to make good judgments and quick decisions
example: Her business acumen turned the small shop into a chain.

definition: excessive admiration or praise
example: The young actor grew weary of the constant adulation.

definition: involving or characterized by active opposition or conflict
example: The negotiations quickly turned adversarial.

definition: friendly, good-natured, and easy to talk to
example: The affable professor invited questions at any hour.

definition: to increase the power, wealth, or status of someone or something
example: The memoir aggrandized even her minor accomplishments.

definition: showing a selfless concern for the well-being of others
example: Her altruistic motives were never in doubt.

definition: having mixed or contradictory feelings about something
example: She felt ambivalent about leaving her hometown.

definition: to make something bad or unsatisfactory better
example: The new policies ameliorated the housing shortage.

definition: belonging to a period other than the one being portrayed
example: The knight with a wristwatch looked anachronistic.

definition: a deep-seated feeling of dislike
example: His antipathy toward reform was well documented.

definition: lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern
example: Voter apathy doomed the reform effort.

definition: a person who settles a dispute or has decisive judgment
example: Critics called her the arbiter of modern taste.

definition: a very typical example of a certain person or thing
example: He is the archetype of the self-made entrepreneur.

definition: having or showing the ability to speak fluently and coherently
example: She was unusually articulate for a first-time witness.

definition: high-sounding language with little meaning
example: The speech was full of bombast and devoid of substance.

definition: to begin to grow or increase rapidly
example: Tech startups have burgeoned across the region.

definition: a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds
example: The cacophony of car horns kept her awake.

definition: given to sudden, unaccountable changes of mood
example: The capricious weather ruined the picnic.

definition: a person or thing that precipitates an event
example: The new law was a catalyst for broader reforms.

definition: a meeting of members of a legislative or political group
example: The caucus nominated its candidate before dawn.

definition: a person who falsely claims expert knowledge or ability
example: The doctor turned out to be a complete charlatan.

definition: a general agreement among a group
example: The committee reached consensus after long debate.

definition: too ready to believe things; gullible
example: Credulous investors lost everything in the scheme.
